name: Rotorua Regional Airport
before:
Sitting on Te Ngae Road about 6km north east of the Rotorua town centre, this is a small regional airport that does a straightforward job well. The terminal is a two-storey building with six tarmac gates, a cafe, a book store and a conference room, so there is enough to keep you occupied for the half hour you are likely to spend here and not much more. General aviation hangars sit to the north and south of the main terminal, with an avgas pump at the southern end of the apron.

Most arrivals come in on Air New Zealand's regional services from Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch. Beyond the scheduled flights, a steady stream of charter and scenic operators work out of the airport, which suits a town where a lot of visitors have come to see the geothermal country and the lakes from above.

The main runway runs 2,114m and is sealed with asphalt. A shorter grass strip runs parallel to it, though the two sit close enough together that only one can be in use at a time. International flights from Sydney ran between 2009 and 2015 but the airport is domestic now.
after:
Sitting on Te Ngae Road about 6km north east of the Rotorua town centre, this is a small regional airport that does a straightforward job well. The airport has a cafe, a conference room and a shop selling books and magazines, so there is enough to keep you occupied for the half hour you are likely to spend here and not much more. General aviation hangars sit to the north and south of the main terminal.

Most arrivals come in on Air New Zealand's regional services from Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch. Beyond the scheduled flights, charter and scenic operators also work from the airport.

The main runway is sealed, with a shorter grass runway parallel to it. Air New Zealand flew to Sydney from 2009 to 2015. Scheduled flights are domestic now, though the airport says it can still handle trans-Tasman charters.

claims.note: Was 'The main runway runs 2,114m and is sealed with asphalt'.
